name: Texas Is the Reason
label: Revelation
lede: Texas Is the Reason made one album, nine songs for Revelation, then broke up in Germany on the eve of a Capitol deal. The record became the label's best seller, and the band keeps coming back on anniversaries.

eras.title: Out of Shelter and 108
eras.text: Norman Brannon had played guitar in Shelter as Norman Arenas, and Chris Daly had drummed in 108, about as devout as hardcore got. With Copper singer Garrett Klahn and bassist Scott Winegard they wrote something warmer and looser, and New York clubs began booking them as the opener everybody showed up early for.

years.src: Revelation Records · Wikipedia: Texas Is the Reason · Anti-Matter
years.h: Chris Leo of the Van Pelt names the band after a Misfits song
years.p: Norman Brannon and Chris Daly add bassist Scott Winegard and singer-guitarist Garrett Klahn. Leo's suggestion, Texas Is the Reason, comes from the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]] song "Bullet", about the JFK assassination.
years.xp:
Revelation's bio traces the members back through Shelter, 108 and Resurrection, a family tree of early-'90s hardcore that sounds nothing like the band they became.

Brannon was still Norman Arenas then, and edited the zine Anti-Matter. He changed his surname legally in 2004, and has written that almost everyone mispronounced Arenas.

years.h: The EP that turns openers into headliners
years.p: The self-titled 1995 EP on Revelation Records moves the band from opening slots to headlining New York shows almost immediately.

years.h: Samuel and Texas Is the Reason split a 7-inch
years.p: Simba Recordings and Art Monk Construction put it out, a small-run record of the kind that got passed around at shows.

eras.title: Nine songs and a question
eras.text: The band made one full-length, Do You Know Who You Are?: nine songs, 37 minutes. The title is reportedly the last thing John Lennon heard on the way to the hospital. Klahn was 21, and the major labels were already calling.

years.src: Revelation Records · Wikipedia: Do You Know Who You Are?
years.h: One album, cut in Baltimore with J. Robbins
years.p: Recorded at Oz Studios in December 1995 with [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] of [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] co-producing and released April 30 on Revelation, Do You Know Who You Are? becomes the label's best-selling record.
years.xp:
Drew Mazurek engineered and mixed at Oz. Vlad Meller mastered at Sony Music Studios in New York, and Glenn Maryansky of Antarctica designed the sleeve. The original runs 37 minutes 42 seconds.

Wikipedia lists it on best-of lists from Kerrang!, NME, Rolling Stone and Spin, at No. 4 on LA Weekly's top 20 emo albums and No. 12 on Rolling Stone's 40 greatest emo albums. AllMusic called Klahn's voice "warm enough to draw one in, while not being overbearing".
play: Do You Know Who You Are?

years.h: A split with the Promise Ring on Jade Tree
years.p: Two of the bands that came to define '90s emo share one record on Jade Tree.

years.h: The majors line up, and Capitol gets the signature
years.p: A year of heavy touring behind the album has labels calling. Texas Is the Reason agrees to sign with Capitol Records.
years.xp: The signing never happened. By Klahn's account to Paste, the Capitol deal was set for the day after the band's last show in Germany.

eras.title: Eight hundred Germans and a way out
eras.text: About ten months after the album came out, Texas Is the Reason stopped. It happened on a European tour with a Capitol deal waiting at home, and the members tell it as a decision, not a blowup.

q: There were eight hundred Germans singing along with us.
years.src: Wikipedia: Texas Is the Reason · Paste: Texas Is The Reason
years.h: The last show is in Bielefeld, Germany
years.p: The final date of the 1997 European tour. Brannon remembers the crowd singing every word, a look over at Daly, and the knowledge that it was over.
years.xp:
Klahn tells it differently. In his version to Paste, the other three talked it over and said: "If tonight's show is great, let's just call it and we'll be done." The split came at Frankfurt airport, with the Capitol deal set for the next day. "It was pretty dramatic, I'll tell you that."

Wikipedia has the band touring Europe on the eve of signing with Capitol. Either way, there was no major-label album. Daly went on to [[Jets to Brazil|675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1]] with [[Blake Schwarzenbach|c7d68007-b688-426f-a496-08467a0a6f44]], and Klahn formed New Rising Sons.

Klahn, thirty years on: "I don't think I'd be talking to you now celebrating a 30-year anniversary had the band continued."

eras.title: Anniversaries only
eras.text: The band came back on round-number anniversaries of the album, and the New York shows sold out fast. Each run was pitched as the last one, and then there was another.

years.p: Ten years after the album, Texas Is the Reason reunite in New York for two nights, November 25 and 26.

years.cap: Music Hall of Williamsburg, Brooklyn, October 10, 2012
years.h: New York again, this time in two rooms
years.p: Irving Plaza and the Music Hall of Williamsburg host the October run, sixteen years after the album.

years.cap: Chris Daly at the Masquerade, Atlanta, March 9, 2013
years.h: Revelation remasters everything and adds two songs nobody had heard
years.p: The Complete Collection gathers all the band's recordings with two previously unreleased songs. A limited North American tour follows.

years.cap: Garrett Klahn at Groezrock, Meerhout, Belgium, April 27, 2013
years.h: Billed as the last one, in London
years.p: Texas Is the Reason bill their August 4 show at the Electric Ballroom as the final one.

years.cap: Scott Winegard at Groezrock, Meerhout, Belgium, April 27, 2013
years.src: Brooklyn Vegan: Texas Is the Reason 20th anniversary
years.h: Twenty years on, in a Brooklyn metal bar
years.p: The album's twentieth anniversary sells out Saint Vitus, and a second night gets added.
years.xp: BrooklynVegan billed the March 15 show as a warm-up for a Jon Bunch tribute in Santa Ana, California, on March 20.

years.src: Billy Penn: RIP · Brooklyn Vegan: Texas Is the Reason 20th anniversary
years.h: A TLA benefit for Jon Bunch's son
years.p: In Philadelphia, Texas Is the Reason play for the late [[Sense Field|8d7bf045-1526-404d-b37c-6f49b714d614]] and [[Further Seems Forever|2bc3d11f-58fe-4adb-bfd9-6d316973005a]] singer Jon Bunch, raising money for his son's college fund.
years.xp:
[[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] and a reunited Sense Field were also on the bill.

The band's statement on the Bunch tributes, as BrooklynVegan printed it: "When you are asked to celebrate the life of a beautiful person that you loved dearly, you just say yes."

eras.title: Nine months in a room
eras.text: Before the 2025 return the band rehearsed for most of a year without telling anyone, then toured farther than it ever had in the '90s. Founder Brannon sat it out and explained why.

years.h: Ten months of rehearsing, and not a word
years.p: Klahn says the band spent nine or ten months getting the fourteen songs of its set right, telling nobody.

years.src: Brooklyn Vegan: Norman Brannon · Paste: Texas Is The Reason
years.h: Brannon stays home, and says why
years.p: Brannon says reviving the band means going back to his mid-'90s life as a closeted gay man, and he doesn't want to. John Herguth plays guitar in his place.
years.xp:
Brannon: "I spent my time in Texas perpetually terrified." He told BrooklynVegan that revisiting something so tied to that time "is just not something I wish to do." He added that there's no bad blood with the band.

Klahn on the new guitarist, to Paste: "Our kid John is like a ray of sunshine coming in."

years.h: Las Vegas, on a bill of reunions
years.p: The band plays Best Friends Forever at the Downtown Las Vegas Events Center, October 10-12, alongside [[Rilo Kiley|eaf6a7ca-105d-4a94-ba02-8c3e4040319a]] and [[Minus the Bear|c1e98e4a-4628-4c89-a7a6-0e0171600b05]].
years.xp: A fan upload shows a full set at Riot Fest on September 21, three weeks earlier.

years.src: Paste: Texas Is the Reason are grateful
years.p: The 2026 run goes to both for the first time, plus Primavera Sound and dates with [[Jimmy Eat World|bbc5b66b-d037-4f26-aecf-0b129e7f876a]] and [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]].
years.xp: Klahn told Paste no new songs are planned unless they come naturally. On the one-album career: "The gods picked us to be one of the bands to release one album."
